page_convo.title: Welcome
page_convo.text: Hi — I'm Jenny, your lab guide. Pick a field below to explore interactive simulations.

page_convo.title: Fields
page_convo.text: Chemistry, Biology, Physics and Engineering each hold multiple projects. Open cards show how many labs are ready.

page_convo.title: Building the suite
page_convo.text: New labs appear as Available when their Godot scenes are ready. Planned means coming soon.

page_convo.title: Chemistry laboratory
page_convo.text: Matter, reactions, equilibrium and energy. Open any Available project to run the simulation.

page_convo.title: Start here
page_convo.text: Gas Laws is a good first stop — ideal gas PV = nRT with a live piston and pressure gauge.

page_convo.title: Biology laboratory
page_convo.text: Cells, populations and ecosystems will live here as we port each simulation.

page_convo.title: Physics laboratory
page_convo.text: Motion and forces. Projectile and particle labs are planned next.

page_convo.title: Engineering laboratory
page_convo.text: Circuits, structures and machines. Circuit Builder and more will unlock here.

page_convo.title: Ideal gas
page_convo.text: Pressure is always calculated from PV = nRT (R = 8.314). The moving particles only illustrate temperature and amount — they do not create the pressure reading.

page_convo.title: Choose a law
page_convo.text: Each law locks two quantities at the moment you select it. You control one slider; the fourth variable follows the law.

page_convo.title: Boyle
page_convo.text: Under Boyle, only volume is free. Compress the piston and watch P rise so that P × V stays constant. Record several points and check the table.

page_convo.title: Charles & Avogadro
page_convo.text: When volume is set by the law, the piston may hit its stops (2–30 L). A status message appears if that happens.

page_convo.title: Record & graph
page_convo.text: Record data points, then compare the constant column across rows. The graph shows points and a prediction curve for the active law.

page_convo.title: Rate law
page_convo.text: We model A → products with rate = k[A]^n for order n = 0, 1 or 2. The curve is the analytical integrated law — not a numerical ODE.

page_convo.title: Curve shape
page_convo.text: Zero-order falls in a straight line; first-order is exponential; second-order decays more slowly at long times. Switch orders and compare.

page_convo.title: Half-life
page_convo.text: The dashed red line marks t½. For first-order, t½ depends only on k; for second-order it also depends on [A]₀.

page_convo.title: Arrhenius
page_convo.text: Enable Arrhenius to set k from temperature and Ea. Raising T increases k and shortens the half-life.

page_convo.title: Three modes
page_convo.text: Weak acid (quadratic Ka), Buffer (Henderson–Hasselbalch), and Strong acid/base for comparison.

page_convo.title: Buffer ratio
page_convo.text: pH ≈ pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]). Equal HA and A⁻ puts you near the pKa — the best buffer region.

page_convo.title: Capacity
page_convo.text: In Buffer mode, add strong acid or base. Small additions barely move pH; large ones break the buffer.

page_convo.title: Acids
page_convo.text: Pick acetic, formic, and others — each has a real Ka. Drag pKa for a custom acid.

page_convo.title: Lotka–Volterra
page_convo.text: Prey grow, predators eat prey and convert them into more predators, predators die. The classic model produces endless cycles.

page_convo.title: Phase portrait
page_convo.text: Plotting prey vs predators often traces a closed loop around the equilibrium (yellow dot).

page_convo.title: Food limit K
page_convo.text: When K is finite, prey cannot explode without predators. Cycles can damp toward equilibrium.

page_convo.title: Try Extinction
page_convo.text: Load the Extinction preset with the floor on — populations that fall below 1 are wiped out for good.

page_convo.title: Continuity
page_convo.text: For steady incompressible flow, Q = A·v is the same at every section. Narrow the pipe and speed must rise.

page_convo.title: Bernoulli
page_convo.text: p/ρ + v²/2 + gz stays constant if you ignore losses. Faster fluid → lower static pressure — that is the venturi effect.

page_convo.title: Head loss
page_convo.text: Friction factor f and length L add head loss h_L, so pressure drops more than the ideal Bernoulli prediction.

page_convo.title: Try Venturi
page_convo.text: Load the Venturi preset, then shrink D₂ — watch v₂ climb and p₂ fall.

page_convo.title: q = ΔT / R
page_convo.text: Heat flux through a wall equals the temperature difference divided by the total thermal resistance. Units: W/m².

page_convo.title: Series resistances
page_convo.text: Each layer adds R = L/k. Convection films add R = 1/h. They all add in series for a single path through the wall.

page_convo.title: Insulation
page_convo.text: Low thermal conductivity k (or thicker L) raises R and lowers q — that is how insulation cuts heat loss in winter.

page_convo.title: Presets
page_convo.text: Compare Winter wall vs Bare brick at the same outdoor temperature — watch q jump when insulation is removed.

page_convo.title: Forward kinematics
page_convo.text: Given joint angles θ₁ and θ₂, FK computes the end-effector (x, y). Move the sliders and watch the arm.

page_convo.title: Inverse kinematics
page_convo.text: Click a point in the workspace to solve for angles that reach it. Some points have two solutions (elbow up / down).

page_convo.title: Workspace
page_convo.text: Reachable points lie between |L₁−L₂| and L₁+L₂ from the base. Outside the grey rings, IK fails.

page_convo.title: Try it
page_convo.text: Load Long reach, then click near the outer ring — then toggle Elbow up to see the other configuration.

page_convo.title: Mechanical advantage
page_convo.text: MA = load / effort. Ideal MA ignores losses; actual MA includes efficiency or friction.

page_convo.title: Lever
page_convo.text: Class 1: fulcrum between load and effort (crowbar). Class 2: load between (wheelbarrow). Class 3: effort between (tweezers).

page_convo.title: Incline
page_convo.text: MA ≈ 1/sin(θ). A gentler ramp needs less effort but a longer path.

page_convo.title: Pulley & wheel
page_convo.text: Pulley MA ≈ number of supporting strands. Wheel-and-axle MA ≈ R/r.

page_convo.title: Equivalence
page_convo.text: Veq = Ca·Va/Cb for a 1:1 reaction. At equivalence, moles of acid and base match.

page_convo.title: Add carefully
page_convo.text: Near the endpoint, use +0.1 mL or +drop. The pH jumps steeply for strong–strong titrations.

page_convo.title: Indicators
page_convo.text: Phenolphthalein suits strong acid–strong base and weak acid–strong base. Methyl orange is better for strong acid–weak base.

page_convo.title: Theory curve
page_convo.text: Turn on the theoretical curve to compare your measured points with the exact charge-balance prediction.

page_convo.title: Kc
page_convo.text: At equilibrium the reaction quotient Q equals Kc. Changing initials, volume or temperature moves the system to a new balance.

page_convo.title: ICE table
page_convo.text: Initial concentrations → extent ξ → equilibrium concentrations. The bars compare I vs E for each species.

page_convo.title: Le Chatelier
page_convo.text: T+ / T− shifts Kc (endo vs exo). Halving V raises all concentrations — gas reactions with Δn ≠ 0 shift composition.

page_convo.title: Haber
page_convo.text: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ is exothermic; cooling favours ammonia. High pressure (small V) also favours products.

page_convo.title: Ideal parabola
page_convo.text: With no drag, range R = v₀² sin(2θ)/g on flat ground is maximised at 45°. The dashed path is that vacuum trajectory.

page_convo.title: Air drag
page_convo.text: Turn up drag c — the real path falls short and is no longer symmetric. Mass then matters because acceleration scales as c/m.

page_convo.title: Cliff & bounce
page_convo.text: Launch from height for a longer flight. Raise bounce e to see multiple landings before rolling stops.

page_convo.title: Gravity presets
page_convo.text: Moon g ≈ 1.62 m/s² stretches the arc dramatically compared with Earth.

page_convo.title: Multi-wire ports
page_convo.text: Any port can take up to 4 wires. Use that to branch from BAT+ to several loads, or join returns to BAT−.

page_convo.title: Switch
page_convo.text: The switch has in+/in− and out+/out−. ON connects in→out for each polarity. OFF opens both.

page_convo.title: Series path
page_convo.text: For a switch to kill an LED, the switch must sit on the only path from BAT+ to BAT−.

page_convo.title: Ports
page_convo.text: Blue = +. Red = −. Grey wire = no current. Yellow = current flowing.

page_convo.title: Kinetic picture
page_convo.text: Particles move freely and bounce off the walls (and each other). Temperature sets how fast they move on average.

page_convo.title: Ideal-like
page_convo.text: With elasticity = 1 and gravity = 0, total kinetic energy stays roughly constant — closer to an ideal gas in a box.

page_convo.title: Dissipation
page_convo.text: Raise gravity and lower elasticity: each bounce loses energy and particles settle toward the bottom.

page_convo.title: Colour
page_convo.text: Bluer = slower; redder = faster. Colour tracks each particle's instantaneous speed.

page_convo.title: SHM
page_convo.text: For small angles the pendulum period is 2π√(L/g), independent of amplitude. The spring period is 2π√(m/k).

page_convo.title: Energy
page_convo.text: KE and PE trade places each quarter cycle. With damping = 0, total energy stays roughly constant.

page_convo.title: Large angles
page_convo.text: At large release angles the pendulum is no longer simple harmonic — period grows slightly.

page_convo.title: Restitution e
page_convo.text: e = 1 is elastic (KE conserved for the pair, ignoring walls). e = 0 is perfectly inelastic — bodies share velocity along the contact normal.

page_convo.title: Momentum
page_convo.text: With no external force along a direction, total momentum in that direction stays constant. Watch px before and after a 1D hit.

page_convo.title: Mass ratio
page_convo.text: A heavy mass hitting a light one at rest transfers a large speed to the light mass in the elastic case.

page_convo.title: Path difference
page_convo.text: Constructive interference where path difference δ = mλ; destructive where δ = (m+½)λ.

page_convo.title: Phase shift
page_convo.text: Adding π phase to source 2 swaps bright and dark fringes along the centre line.

page_convo.title: Separation
page_convo.text: Wider source separation packs more fringes into the same screen region.

page_convo.title: Media-first world
page_convo.text: Food (green) and waste (grey) live on a grid. Temperature, pH, viscosity and oxygen change how well cells eat and move.

page_convo.title: Life cycle
page_convo.text: Each tick a cell senses food, metabolizes, moves up the gradient, grows, and may divide with a mutated genome — or die from starvation or age.

page_convo.title: Four types
page_convo.text: Coccus is balanced, Bacillus is an efficient feeder, Spirillum is a fast forager, Vibrio is a hardy middle ground. Watch which type wins in each preset.

page_convo.title: Try this
page_convo.text: Load Hot Spring, press Play, then cool the temperature toward 37 °C — population and energy charts should respond. Click a cell to possess it.

page_convo.title: Presets
page_convo.text: Aqueous is a friendly broth. Hot Spring is warmer and leaner. Agar is viscous with richer food — motion slows, colonies persist.

page_convo.title: Food web compartments
page_convo.text: Nutrients feed producers. Herbivores eat producers. Carnivores eat herbivores. Death and inefficient eating build detritus, which recycles back to nutrients.

page_convo.title: Energy pyramid
page_convo.text: Each trophic step keeps only a fraction of the energy (efficiency). Upper levels are thinner — that is why the pyramid narrows.

page_convo.title: Nutrient bloom
page_convo.text: High nutrient input can fuel a producer bloom. Without enough grazers, the system tilts toward plants and detritus.

page_convo.title: Overfish
page_convo.text: High carnivore death (or predation pressure) can crash the top level and let herbivores surge — then overgraze producers.

page_convo.title: Selection
page_convo.text: Individuals closer to the environmental optimum have higher fitness and leave more offspring. The mean trait moves toward z*.

page_convo.title: Mutation
page_convo.text: Mutation adds variation. Without it, selection uses up diversity and adaptation to a moving target stalls.

page_convo.title: Drift
page_convo.text: In small populations, random sampling (drift) can overpower weak selection — try the Weak/drift preset.

page_convo.title: Moving target
page_convo.text: When the optimum shifts each generation, the population must evolve continuously to keep up — a simple model of environmental change.

page_convo.title: Competition
page_convo.text: When two species share resources, each reduces the other's growth. Competition coefficients α measure how strongly that happens.

page_convo.title: Competitive exclusion
page_convo.text: If niches are nearly identical (α ≈ 1), one species usually drives the other to zero — Gause's principle.

page_convo.title: Coexistence
page_convo.text: When each species inhibits itself more than its competitor (niche partitioning), a stable coexistence equilibrium can appear.

page_convo.title: Isoclines
page_convo.text: On the phase plane, teal and violet lines are zero-growth isoclines. Their crossing (yellow) is the predicted equilibrium.

page_convo.title: Reaction types
page_convo.text: Synthesis, decomposition, single/double replacement, combustion, acid–base, and simple redox — each catalogue entry is tagged with its type.

page_convo.title: Limiting reactant
page_convo.text: The reactant that runs out first limits how far the reaction can go. Lower one slider and watch products shrink.

page_convo.title: Builder
page_convo.text: Pick two species and Find reaction — if a known pair exists in the catalogue, that reaction loads automatically.

page_convo.title: Try this
page_convo.text: Open AgCl precipitate, set AgNO₃ high and NaCl low — NaCl becomes limiting and leftover silver nitrate remains.

page_convo.title: Free mix
page_convo.text: Pick up to three species and Run free mix. Exact reactant sets from the catalogue will load; unknown combinations report no reaction — chemistry stays honest.
